title: 2026-11-17_Remaiten_Botnet_Investigation_7b5
description: You are an incident responder tasked with investigating a compromised network where the Remaiten botnet malware has been detected. The malware targets routers and IoT devices, performing telnet scanning to infect new victims and establishing command-and-control (C2) communication. Your goal is to identify and analyze the malicious activities, understand the infection vector, and contain the threat.
outcomes: Identify suspicious services and their behaviors.
Analyze systemd timers and services for persistence mechanisms.
Investigate network communication to uncover C2 channels.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: You are an incident responder tasked with investigating a compromised network where the Remaiten botnet malware has been detected. The malware targets routers and IoT devices, performing telnet scanning to infect new victims and establishing command-and-control (C2) communication. Your goal is to identify and analyze the malicious activities, understand the infection vector, and contain the threat.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: Access the sandbox via the provided cloud environment.
levels.local_content: Local sandbox access is not required for this scenario.

levels.title: Suspicious Service Discovery
levels.content: Security monitoring has detected an unusual network-facing component on the compromised host. Investigate the running services and identify the service responsible for sending beacon periodically to the C2 Server.
levels.solution:
1. List all services:
```bash
systemctl list-units --type=service --all
```
2. Identify suspicious services:
Look for services with unusual names or descriptions. Pay attention to services that are not part of standard system services.
3. Check the status of suspicious services:
```bash
systemctl status <service_name>
```
4. Identify the beacon service:
The beacon service is likely to have a description related to system health or network diagnostics.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use `systemctl list-units --type=service --all` to list all services.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for services with unusual names or descriptions that do not match standard system services.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Use `systemctl status <service_name>` to check the status and description of suspicious services.

levels.title: C2 Communication Discovery (Port)
levels.content: An unfamiliar network service appears to be involved in unauthorized communication with an external system. Investigate the service and determine the network port associated with this communication.
levels.solution:
1. Inspect the beacon service configuration:
```bash
systemctl cat bot-beacon.service
```
2. Identify the ExecStart path:
The ExecStart field in the service configuration points to the script responsible for the beacon activity.
3. Examine the beacon script:
```bash
cat /usr/local/lib/.botcache/beacon.sh
```
4. Identify the C2 port:
The beacon script contains the port number used for communication with the C2 server.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use `systemctl cat bot-beacon.service` to inspect the service configuration.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for the ExecStart field in the service configuration to find the path to the beacon script.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Examine the beacon script to find the port number used for communication with the C2 server.

levels.title: Persistence Discovery for C2 Beaconing Service
levels.content: Investigators suspect how the C2 beacon service automatically resumes after the system starts and continues to execute periodically. Determine which system component is responsible for scheduling this activity.
levels.solution:
1. List all timers:
```bash
systemctl list-timers --all
```
2. Identify the timer associated with the beacon service:
Look for timers with names related to the beacon service.
3. Inspect the timer configuration:
```bash
systemctl cat <timer_name>
```
4. Identify the timer responsible for scheduling the beacon service:
The timer configuration will show the schedule and the service it triggers.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use `systemctl list-timers --all` to list all timers.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for timers with names related to the beacon service.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Use `systemctl cat <timer_name>` to inspect the timer configuration and identify the service it triggers.
